title: Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's
oneLiner: The one Australian jurisdiction with reservation has had the cheapest domestic gas.
body: Since 2006 Western Australia has negotiated a 15 per cent domestic reservation into the approval of each LNG project. Through the east-coast price spikes of 2017 and 2022 its domestic wholesale prices stayed a fraction of eastern levels.
contextBackground: Western Australia is a natural comparison because it is the only part of the country that has run the policy, and because its gas market is physically separate from the east coast's.
contextDisagreement: The price gap is agreed. The dispute is causation: Western Australia also has abundant, cheap offshore gas and a small domestic market, and compliance with its reservation has been described as poor, so the policy may deserve less credit than it gets.

evidenceItems.citation: Government of Western Australia, Western Australian Domestic Gas Policy
Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, Gas Inquiry — east-coast and western price comparisons

otherClaim.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices

claimItself.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices
claimItself.oneLiner: Australia has decided to reserve gas for domestic buyers. The question now is whether the scheme, as designed and then softened, will do what it was announced to do.
claimItself.body: In May 2026 the federal government announced that Queensland's three LNG export ventures must reserve a share of export volumes for Australian users from July 2027, with contracts signed before 22 December 2025 exempt. In September 2026 the rule was recast around forecast domestic demand rather than a flat share of exports. The government says prices will fall; it will not say by how much.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Because export contracts signed before 22 December 2025 are exempt, the scheme reaches too little gas to move prices for years

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Mandatory reservation will deter investment in new gas supply and worsen the shortfall it is meant to fix

otherClaim.title: Western Australia's low domestic gas prices owe more to abundant, cheap offshore gas and a small market than to reservation

claimItself.title: Western Australia's low domestic gas prices owe more to abundant, cheap offshore gas and a small market than to reservation
claimItself.oneLiner: The precedent may show geology, not policy.
claimItself.body: Western Australia's LNG projects draw on large offshore fields with low production costs, and its domestic market is a fraction of the east coast's. Critics of the comparison argue those conditions would produce low prices with or without a reservation rule, so the policy cannot be credited with the gap.
